conviction_note: Slight long lean (p_up 53 on an abs move of 19, so (2*0.53-1)*19 = +1.14). It rests on a cloud-communications guide that management called conservative because it excludes Salesforce and the five newest enterprise deals, on a short position that has grown to about 16% of shares and 7 days to cover, and on a 17.6% fall over 20 days that lowered the bar. It is held near 50 because this stock sold its last beat-and-raise by 29% and the put skew (+4.2 vol points) leans the other way. The findings sum to +2.6. The scaled number is smaller because the lean is mostly inference, not a new primary number.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue $231-235m and non-GAAP EPS $0.45-0.49, adjusted EBITDA $32-34m (company guide, Q2 release https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1514416/000151441626000055/q220268kexh991.htm, 2026-07-29). FY2026 guide: revenue $900-910m, cloud communications $622-626m, adjusted EBITDA $123-125m, EPS $1.71-1.79. Street: revenue $233.1m (Benzinga) and $233.15m (MarketBeat), both at the guide midpoint. EPS consensus is disputed, $0.42 (Benzinga) against $0.47 (MarketBeat), and one aggregator shows $0.23, which is probably GAAP. So revenue is sourced to the guide plus two agreeing estimates; EPS is guide-sourced only. Last quarter the company beat the revenue consensus by about 1.2% ($219.9m vs $217.3m).
positioning_check: Short interest 5,117,810 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, about 15.9% of shares outstanding, 7.02 days to cover. It has risen from 4,362,879 (2026-08-31) and 4,723,069 (2026-09-30) (equibles.com/stocks/band/shortinterest, read 2026-10-28). Part of it is probably convertible-arbitrage hedging against the $316m 0% notes due 2032 issued in Q2 2026, so not all of it is directional. Skew is +4.16 vol points (25d put IV over call IV): a modest downside lean. Put/call open-interest ratio is 0.36. The ATM spread is 36% of mid, so the 18.35% event-implied move is indicative only. Into the print the stock is down 17.6% over 20 days, down 36% from its 52-week high and up 290% from its 52-week low. Consensus rating is Hold with a $59.83 target; Morgan Stanley initiated Equal-Weight at $56 on 2026-10-16 and BofA Neutral at $60 on 2026-09-16.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call (2026-07-29) management said the H2 cloud-communications guide ($622-626m FY) assumes growth 'slightly less than the first half growth rate' and called it conservative, because it excludes the Salesforce Agentforce Contact Center ramp and the five newest $1m+ enterprise wins. They also said two 2025 customers would exit 2026 at nearly twice their originally estimated contract value. Salesforce has since announced (2026-09-16) a rollout to 25+ countries 'this fall'. That sets up a fourth consecutive raise of the FY revenue/EBITDA guide. The bar is the guide midpoint ($233m Q3 revenue, $905m FY).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 (2026-04-30): beat and raise, +52.1%. Q2 2026 (2026-07-29): revenue beat (+1.2% vs consensus), FY revenue and EBITDA raised, FY EPS trimmed for share count, political cut from $15m to $13m: -29.3%. So a raise alone has not protected the stock; the read is on the quality of cloud-communications growth and the EPS line.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus sits exactly at the guide midpoint ($233.1m), so the street has not modelled the excluded Salesforce and new-deal ramps. A market pricing a raise would not have the stock 17.6% lower over 20 days with Hold initiations ('price already reflects much of the growth', Morgan Stanley 2026-10-16). Pricing it would look like a consensus above the guide range.
findings.independence: Salesforce/Bandwidth international rollout release, 2026-09-16, a different document: https://techintelpro.com/news/Cloud/Cloud-AI/bandwidth-salesforce-expand-global-rollout-of-native-contact-center. The September 2026 investor deck (8-K 2026-09-15) repeats the guide midpoints without raising them: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1514416/000151441626000069/a2026bandwidthinvestorpr.htm

findings.finding: Q2 Voice Solutions revenue was $121m, up only 9% year on year, a slowdown from Q1 that management blamed on enterprise ramp timing. The AI-voice narrative that carried the stock from about $13 to $78 needs voice growth to reaccelerate in Q3. A second quarter near 9% is the most likely trigger for a repeat of the -29% Q2 reaction, even with total revenue at the guide. What would have to go right elsewhere: messaging (commercial +18% in Q2) and software services (+66%) are already carrying the growth.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 print, where voice decelerated to 9%, moved -29.3% despite a total-revenue beat and raise. Q1 2026, with strong AI-voice commentary, moved +52.1%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the 20-day fall and the Hold initiations reflect doubt about growth. The specific line (voice growth reaccelerating or not) is not in any consensus aggregator, which carries only total revenue and EPS. Sized small because a crowded short (16% of shares, 7 DTC) dampens a negative.
findings.independence: This shares the Q2 transcript with finding 1 but reads a different line (Voice Solutions reported growth vs cloud-communications guide conservatism). The two can both be true: the guide can be raised while voice stays slow. Nothing independent points the same way.

findings.finding: The 2026 midterm cycle is generating record-looking political texting: 'tens of billions' of political texts (Fox 13, 2026-10-05) and phones 'blowing up' in Alaska (Alaska Public, 2026-10-15). Bandwidth's own political assumption was cut to $13m for FY2026 (from $15m), with only about $1m recognised in Q2 and the rest principally in H2. Political upside beyond that assumption would show in Q3 programmable messaging and in the Q4 guide (the election is 2026-11-03). Net of the rest: $13m is about 1.4% of the $905m FY revenue, so even a 50% political beat is under 1% of revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The political cut from $15m to $13m was one of the cited reasons for the -29.3% Q2 2026 reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: The company guided political down three months ago and no aggregator tracks Bandwidth's share of campaign SMS. If it were priced, the political cut would have been reversed in estimates; consensus is still at the guide. This is an industry proxy, not a company number, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Alaska Public Media, 2026-10-15, a separate outlet: https://alaskapublic.org/news/politics/elections/2026-10-15/ahead-of-the-midterms-alaskans-phones-are-blowing-up-with-political-calls-and-texts. Neither source gives a 2026 total volume figure.

findings.finding: On 2026-07-25 Bandwidth amended its Bank of America credit agreement to double the annual restricted-payments cap from $20m to $40m (or 20% of TTM EBITDA if greater), subject to a leverage cushion. The company bought back $15m of stock in Q2 at $57.06 and $20m year to date, and also repurchased $20.8m of 2028 converts at a discount (8-K 2026-08-03). With the stock now at $50, below its Q2 buyback price, a larger or new buyback authorization announced with Q3 is a plausible capital-return item.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No standalone buyback announcement in the baseline history; the Q2 buyback disclosure came alongside a -29.3% reaction, so it was not sufficient on its own.
findings.why_not_priced: The covenant change sits in an Item 1.01 summary of a results-day 8-K that the wire coverage ignored; none of the previews mention buyback capacity. If it were priced, there would be sell-side discussion of a new authorization; none was found. This is inferred from covenant arithmetic, not stated intent, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: The Q2 transcript's buyback detail ($15m at $57.06), a different document: https://www.webull.com/news/15364520829936640

findings.finding: Positioning into the print is short-heavy and de-risked. Short interest rose from 4.36m shares (2026-08-31) to 5.12m (2026-10-15), about 16% of shares outstanding at 7.0 days to cover. The stock fell 17.6% over 20 days on a tech/AI sell-off (10-year yield above 5.27%), Morgan Stanley's Equal-Weight initiation at $56 and three single-day drops of 8-14% (10-08, 10-16, 10-22) with no company news found. A guide that is merely firm meets a crowded short and a lowered bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 +52.1% came off a depressed base. Q2 2026 -29.3% came after a run to about $72 (17 July), the opposite setup to today.
findings.why_not_priced: The +4.2 put skew and the 20-day fall price downside. What is not priced is the squeeze mechanism if the guide is raised: 7 days to cover against 780k average volume. Part of the short is probably a hedge against the new 0% 2032 converts, which caps the squeeze.
findings.independence: The macro and initiation context (koalagains, 2026-10-16): https://koalagains.com/daily-top-movers/top-losers/details/f3904807-0328-4b06-abb1-8ac81c36f641. The 10-08 drop with no catalyst (MarketBeat): https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-bandwidth-nasdaq-band-stock-falls-88-whats-next-2026-10-08/

outside_window.finding: Peers (Twilio, Sinch) report Q3 2026 after Bandwidth (Twilio last year on 10-30 after the close, Sinch in early November), so no peer read-through is available before this print. Any CPaaS read-through lands after the exit.
General Counsel Asbill retires 2026-12-31 (successor Emily Harlan in place since 2026-09-01). The transition is orderly, says nothing about the quarter and is dated after the window.

searched_and_found_nothing: Cause of the 2026-10-22 -14.3% and 2026-10-14 -9.7% single-day drops: MarketBeat headlines only, no company 8-K or news found (EDGAR shows no 8-K after 2026-09-15)
Q3-specific sell-side previews or estimate revisions in October 2026: none found beyond the Morgan Stanley initiation
Peer prints after Bandwidth last spoke (Twilio, Sinch Q3 2026): not yet reported
Quantified 2026 political SMS volume or FEC texting-vendor spend: no 2026 total published
Microsoft Teams / Zoom customer concentration: not discussed on the Q2 call or in the September deck
Insider Form 4s since August: routine vesting-related sales plus one 1,500-share director 10b5-1 sale on 2026-10-16 at $49.04; no cluster

rejected_candidates.detail: Merged into the positioning finding (5); it is wire context for the 20-day fall, not a separate fact about the print.

rejected_candidates.detail: The Form 4 itself shows a pre-scheduled 10b5-1 sale of 1,500 shares; the document rules out a discretionary signal. Recorded so the panel can see it.

rejected_candidates.detail: Already in the Q3 EPS guide ($0.45-0.49) that the bar uses and already reacted to on 2026-07-29; it informs the EPS bar dispute rather than standing as a separate finding.

baseline_tension: A mild long lean against a modest put skew (+4.2) and the reaction function (the last beat-and-raise sold 29%), and with the -17.6% 20-day run-up, which the crowded short and the conservative guide argue overshot. p_up is held at 53 for that reason.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a reaction; this name sold a beat-and-raise by 29% last quarter): conservative-guide finding cut from +2.0 to +1.5; p_up from 54 to 53.
Rule 7 (a crowded short shrinks a negative; 16% of shares short, 7 DTC): voice-deceleration negative cut from -1.0 to -0.8.
Rules 5 and 9 (a proxy is filed small; a segment is sized net of the rest): political-texting finding cut from +0.7 to +0.4, since political is about 1.4% of FY revenue.
'What has worked' (covenant arithmetic is inference, not a document): buyback finding cut from +0.8 to +0.5.
Positioning finding left at +1.0; abs_move_pct left at 19 (the understatement lesson argues against shrinking it).
